content: 1. The metabolism of drugs through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 can be significantly altered by various agents, necessitating careful monitoring and dose adjustments. For example, fedratinib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, and dose adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 2. Cobicistat and darunavir both increase the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 3. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. If co-administration is necessary, frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is essential, with fentanyl dose adjustments until stable effects are achieved. 4. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the levels or effects of fentanyl administered intranasally or transdermally by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation is necessary, with dose adjustments as needed. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of flunisolide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dose titration of antidepressants may be necessary. 10. Darunavir increases the levels of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Alternatives should be considered if available. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Start with the lowest recommended dose of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and titrate as needed. 15. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of cobicistat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dose titration of antidepressants may be necessary. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (the major active metabolite of fostamatinib). Monitor for toxicities that may require dose reduction. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406. Monitor for toxicities that may necessitate dose reduction. 19. Garlic decreases the levels of darunavir through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects from gefitinib. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects from gefitinib. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Darunavir decreases the effects of glimepiride through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 24. Darunavir may increase or decrease the levels of glipizide. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors has been reported. 25. Darunavir decreases the effects of glyburide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 26. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Green tea and darunavir may increase the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 34. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of darunavir. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. 36. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Alternatives should be considered if available. Reduced formation of active metabolites and increased toxicity of active metabolites may occur. 38. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone also increases the levels of darunavir. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of imipramine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dose titration of antidepressants may be necessary. 42. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases the levels of darunavir. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 45. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 46. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 47. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 48. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin glargine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 49. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin glulisine through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 50. Darunavir decreases the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 51. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin lispro through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 52. Darunavir decreases the effects of insulin NPH through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 53. Darunavir decreases the effects of regular human insulin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 54. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 55. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
